adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Indonesia – Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's national-framework overview, the position a visitor to Maluku stands under: private same-sex conduct is not itself criminalised nationally, but the penal code as amended on 6 December 2022 criminalises sexual activity outside marriage effective 2 January 2026, with unmarried partners facing up to one year in prison if an immediate family member lodges a complaint; because same-sex marriage is not recognised, all sexual activity by same-sex couples falls within that outside-marriage restriction. Legal gender recognition is available only after sex-reassignment surgery plus judicial approval, and only 'male' and 'female' sex descriptors are recognised, with no third-gender or X marker; since June 2021 the Ministry of Home Affairs has run outreach issuing transgender Indonesians electronic ID cards (in nine provinces) as the document route. National law provides no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protections and the Constitution is silent on sexual orientation and gender identity; on 14 December 2017 the Constitutional Court rejected 5-4 a petition to criminalise homosexuality, and the Sharia-based criminalisation outlier is Aceh, not Maluku. The page records that Indonesia voted against the UN independent expert on sexual orientation and gender identity and that a 2023 Pew Research survey found 95% of Indonesians oppose same-sex marriage.
